title: JavaScript
description: Master JavaScript step-by-step. Clean, bullet-pointed, practical lessons designed for modern students.

lessons.title: JavaScript Intro & Role
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 What is JavaScript?

  • Language of the Web: Runs inside every browser natively.
  • Interpreted & Dynamic: High-level language supporting OOP, functional & event-driven paradigms.

💡 Role in Web Dev

  • HTML: Structure of the page.
  • CSS: Presentation & layout.
  • JavaScript: Behavior, interactivity & logic.

🎯 Real-World Usage

  • Interactive forms, live notifications, single-page apps (React/Next.js), & Node.js backend servers.

📝 Quick Task

  • Open Browser DevTools Console (F12) and type console.log("Hello JS!").

lessons.title: JavaScript Hello World
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Displaying Output

  • console.log(): Outputs text/data to developer console.
  • alert(): Displays a browser popup modal box.
  • document.write(): Writes directly to HTML output stream.

💡 Script Tag Location

  • Placed inside <script>...</script> tags at bottom of <body>.

📝 Quick Task

  • Log your favorite movie title using console.log().

lessons.title: JavaScript Syntax
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Syntax Basics

  • Statements: Instructions executed by the browser.
  • Semicolons: Optional in modern JS, but recommended to separate statements.
  • Case Sensitivity: myVar and myvar are different variables!

💡 Comments

  • Single-line: // comment
  • Multi-line: /* comment */

📝 Quick Task

  • Write a statement logging two numbers added together.

lessons.title: JavaScript Variables (let, const, var)
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Variable Declarations

  • const: For variables whose value should NOT change (Default choice!).
  • let: For variables whose value WILL change later.
  • var: Legacy declaration (Avoid using in modern JS!).

💡 Scope Difference

  • let & const are block-scoped {...}.
  • var is function-scoped (can lead to unexpected bugs).

⚠️ Common Mistake

  • ❌ Mistake: Reassigning a const variable -> TypeError!
  • ✅ Fix: Use let if re-assignment is needed.

📝 Quick Task

  • Declare a const for birth year and a let for age. Print both.

lessons.title: JavaScript Data Types
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Primitive Types

  • string: Text wrapped in quotes ("Hello")
  • number: Integers & floating decimals (10, 3.14)
  • boolean: true or false
  • undefined: Variable declared but not assigned
  • null: Intentional absence of value
  • symbol & bigint: Advanced primitives

💡 Reference Types

  • Object, Array, Function

📝 Quick Task

  • Check the type of typeof 42 using console.log().

lessons.title: JavaScript Operators
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Essential Operators

  • Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ** (exponent)
  • Comparison: === (strict equality), !==, >, <
  • Logical: && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT)

⚠️ Crucial Tip

  • Always use strict equality === instead of loose equality == to avoid unintended type coercion.

📝 Quick Task

  • Compare 5 === "5" vs 5 == "5" in console.

lessons.title: JavaScript Functions & Arrow Functions
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Function Declarations

  • Re-usable blocks of code that perform specific tasks.
  • Arrow Functions (ES6): Concise syntax () => {}.

💡 Implicit Return

  • Single-line arrow functions return automatically: const add = (a, b) => a + b;

📝 Quick Task

  • Write an arrow function square = (n) => n * n and test it.
lessons.tryItDefault:
const multiply = (a, b) => a * b;
console.log(multiply(4, 5));

lessons.title: JavaScript Objects
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Key-Value Collections

  • Store collections of data in key: value format.
  • Created using curly braces { key: value }.
  • Properties accessed via dot notation obj.key or bracket obj["key"].

📝 Quick Task

  • Create a user object with name and role. Print the role.

lessons.title: JavaScript Arrays & Iteration
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Ordered Lists

  • Store multiple values in a single variable: [item1, item2].
  • Zero-indexed (first element is at index 0).

💡 High-Order Methods

  • .map(): Transform every item and return new array.
  • .filter(): Keep only items matching condition.
  • .forEach(): Loop through elements.

📝 Quick Task

  • Filter an array [10, 20, 30] to keep numbers > 15.

lessons.title: JavaScript DOM Manipulation
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Document Object Model

  • Tree structure representing HTML elements on the page.
  • Allows JS to dynamically modify content, styles, & attributes.

💡 Key Methods

  • document.querySelector(selector): Select element.
  • element.textContent = "New Text": Modify text.
  • element.style.color = "blue": Modify styles.

📝 Quick Task

  • Select heading with id 'title' and change its text color to blue.
lessons.tryItDefault: console.log("DOM manipulation connects JS with HTML!");

lessons.title: JavaScript Events & Listeners
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Responding to User Interaction

  • Events: click, submit, keydown, mouseover, scroll.
  • element.addEventListener('event', callback)

💡 Event Object (e)

  • e.preventDefault(): Stops default form submission page reload.

📝 Quick Task

  • Attach a click listener to a button element logging "Button clicked!".
lessons.tryItDefault: console.log("Event listeners listen for user clicks!");

lessons.title: Async / Await & Fetch API
lessons.explanationHtml:
📌 Asynchronous Execution

  • Prevents app freezing during network requests / database queries.
  • async: Defines asynchronous function.
  • await: Pauses execution until Promise resolves.

💡 Fetch API

  • fetch(url) returns a Promise containing Response object.
  • Always convert to JSON: await res.json().

📝 Quick Task

  • Write an async function that fetches data from a test URL and logs result.
